scope: Three goals on one local iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26) and two on a phone-use cloud Android phone. Not a general phone-agent evaluation.
timing: From the first observation through the final DONE, including Jev requests, text-helper calls, device verbs, re-observations and (for the About run) a screenshot per step. Excludes simulator boot and the examples' own setup/verification walks.
jev: typesafe-ai/jev via the Vercel AI Gateway (free tier)
text_model: meta/llama-4-scout via the Vercel AI Gateway (free tier)

retained_failures.note: Reported done in 2 decisions and the switch read back on — but the run had started ON the target screen: goHome() is a no-op on the local simulator backend (confirmed with a probe: Settings still frontmost 2.8 s later). The example now relaunches Settings to its root; HOME was removed from the action space.

(1) 25 decisions of OPEN_APP on an app that failed to launch: the SDK lists third-party apps as "Name (bundle)" and Apple's own apps not at all, and nothing stopped a repeating failure. Fixed by parsing names, adding the built-in Apple apps, and a stop after the same action fails twice. (2) BLOCKED at 0.51 vs OPEN_APP 0.30 while the app head had Contacts at 1.00: the operation question could not see which apps existed. The app names are now part of the shared state. (3) A run that started on the previous run's contact card EDITED that contact's last name and passed a naive unique-name check. The example now starts on the list and the failure is kept as a warning about verification design.

retained_failures.goal: Bold Text on a phone-use cloud phone
retained_failures.note: The first RPC timed out (daemon under load from a concurrent benchmark). Cloud calls now go through resilient(): re-open on SESSION_NOT_FOUND, one retry for read-only calls, never for mutations. No cloud timing is claimed.

Immediate HTTP 503 from the gateway: the Android app list (223 packages) had gone into the request whole, 24 KB. looksLikeAndroid had rejected the listing because 'android' has no dot. Fixed; the tiny and head-less requests succeeded throughout, so it was size, not the service.
